dedupe_keys.name: invert ee lab building stock energy demand and policy simulation tu wien

description: Invert/EE-Lab is a dynamic bottom-up techno-socio-economic model from TU Wien's Energy Economics Group that evaluates how policy packages affect total energy demand, energy carrier mix, CO2 reductions and costs for space heating, cooling, hot water and lighting in buildings. It rests on highly disaggregated building stock data, with each segment described by geometry, component U-values, construction period and heating and hot water systems, and holds a database for all EU-28 countries. First built in the Altener project Invert from 2003 to 2005 and re-programmed in 2010 to represent the varied decision makers in the building sector, it has been extended with Invert/Opt optimisation, Invert/Acc accounting and Invert/CC cost curves, and used for EU-28 scenarios to 2030, 2050 and 2080. Coverage: EU-28 building stocks. Access: through the research group; maps and a datamapper present results. Licence: not stated. Caveats: the model itself is not published for download. Simulation uses: long-term renovation and heating system transition scenarios. Related records: Hotmaps building stock maps and TABULA typologies.
